name: MetaEncoder v1

lineage.base_model: muse_glimmer architecture (card: transformers >= 5.15 is the first release with muse_glimmer; MuseGlimmerModel loaded via AutoModel)

purpose: Multimodal embedding model for image-text, video and document retrieval with task instructions, plus a 'decide' call that answers Jev-style yes/no, choice and score questions about a state with probabilities (card).

license.name: not stated on the v1 card
license.notes: HF metadata of facebook/meta-encoder-v1 carries no license field and the card read has no license section. The earlier facebook/meta-encoder (2026-09-30) is tagged apache-2.0 by the HF API, and its card (read through a summarizing page fetch, files gated, raw LICENSE 401) says Apache 2.0 inherited from the base Muse-Glimmer-30B plus the base model's Usage Policy; the license text itself was not read for either repo.

architecture.kind: large multimodal decoder-style encoder (muse_glimmer), 6656-dimensional L2-normalised embeddings

variants.notes: card says one 80 GB GPU holds the model in bf16

earlier release, 29.8B parameters, gated; card (page fetch): bi-encoder made by contrastive fine-tuning of meta-models/Muse-Glimmer-30B, paper arXiv 2610.11316, 85 downloads and 35 likes in the month shown

pc-16gb.notes: 57 GB BF16 would need heavy offload for an embedding workload

mac-64gb+.notes: 57 GB BF16 against about 52 GB GPU share on 64 GB; needs a quant

other: Transformers >= 5.15 with MetaEncoder wrapper (encode, retrieve, decide)

benchmarks.name: NanoBEIR (multilingual text retrieval)
benchmarks.variant: facebook/meta-encoder (first release, not v1); Qwen3-VL-Embedding-8B 0.6061, WeMM-Embedding-9B 0.6175

strengths: One model for text, image, video and document embeddings and for structured decisions
weaknesses: 57 GB in BF16 and 6656-dimensional vectors make it unsuitable for local retrieval on our hardware classes
Benchmarks only as an image in the card
License not stated on the v1 card
soft.maturity: Meta; 687 downloads on the HF API 2026-11-19.

tona_fit.reason: Too large for every hardware class except as a marginal 64 GB Mac case, and the vector size and cost are out of proportion for local document search; smaller visual retrievers (EVIE, ml-embed, Qwen3-VL embedding) cover the use case.

sources.note: first-release card via a summarizing page fetch (raw README, config.json and LICENSE return HTTP 401, no mirror found); benchmark table and usage from there
metadata: apache-2.0 tag, base_model meta-models/Muse-Glimmer-30B, 59.58 GB, created 2026-09-30
